whisper.text: ...phrenomenon related to our own neural systems. Sensing this, I pursued biofeedback experiments with the intent to use my brainwaves, heartbeat, and respiration readings as voltage control for video effects and image transformations. This was accomplished by first plugging myself into a Beckman EEG machine, a brainwave monitor, and other devices, spending hours viewing film loops and breathing in sync with a film motion. The intent was basically to create a loop between the viewer and a projection. I chose waves because I surf, and because of the wave nature of energy. It seemed a suitable metaphor for the work I was doing. These early biofeedback experiments were undoubtedly one of the predecessor forms to virtual reality interfaces, which placed the brainwaves in a virtual reality environment and the viewer directly in touch with a virtual computer-generated world which interacts directly with the participant.
